Subject: Re: RFP: Schedule for retention handback + sample export

Hi all — attaching the schedule and a sample schema (see attachments). Below is an operational playbook summary we can commit to in an SLA addendum.

Operational playbook (summary):
1) Request intake and validation (T0)
   - Customer raises export request via support portal or signed request to legal-requests@redwood.com
   - We validate scope (time range, event types, redaction policy) within 4 business hours

2) Sampling export (if requested)
   - SLA: 8 business hours from validation to delivery for sample extracts (<= 5GB)
   - Format: NDJSON lines, UTF-8, fields described in evidence-sample-schema.jsonl attachment
   - Integrity: Each NDJSON line includes an event_id, timestamp (ISO8601), request_id, model_version, and correlating session_id

3) Full export
   - SLA: 72 hours for full exports up to 500GB; larger exports scheduled with a mutually agreed window (typical lead time 5 business days)
   - Format: gzipped TAR containing: 
     - events.ndjson (primary records)
     - manifest.json (file list, SHA256 checksums, sequence start/end tokens)
     - metadata.csv (map of redaction flags and retention tier)

4) Delivery and tamper-evidence
   - Delivery options: S3 presigned PUT, secure SFTP push, or encrypted AWS Snowball for very large datasets
   - We generate manifest.json signed with a Redwood HMAC key (rotated quarterly). Customer may request an escrow HMAC verification step with their key (we support exchanging public keys during onboarding)
   - We include an MD5 and SHA256 hash for each file; we also provide a signed timestamp entry and an optional notarized record (pdf) for legal hold cases

5) Chain-of-custody and packaging
   - We provide a chain-of-custody CSV listing operators involved, timestamps for package creation, transfer attempts, and successful receipt acknowledgements
   - For repeatability we include a replay script (python) that validates line counts and checksums (script is a helper, not an execution policy)

Schema & sampling specifics (from attachment):
- evidence-sample-schema.jsonl: sample NDJSON schema includes 42 fields; we can provide a slim view with the 10 canonical audit fields if required (event_id, event_type, ts, user_id, api_key_id, request_id, session_id, model_version, prompt_len, response_len)
- Retention tiers: we will map customer retention windows (90/365/730) to internal hot/warm/cold tiers; exports reflect the stored timestamp and tier label for each record

Acceptance criteria & SLA penalties:
- If a sample SLA (8h) is missed more than twice in a rolling 90-day window, we will provide a credit against the next monthly invoice for the exported unit-hours (formula in spreadsheet)

Attachments: retention-handoff-schedule.xlsx (detailed timeline + calendar), evidence-sample-schema.jsonl (NDJSON sample)

I can also provide a small example manifest inline if helpful — sample manifest list would look like: 
  {
    "files": [
      {"name": "events.ndjson.gz", "sha256": "...", "size_bytes": 23452345},
      {"name": "manifest.json", "sha256": "...", "size_bytes": 3421} 
    ],
    "export_range": {"start": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", "end": "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"},
    "created_at": "2026-06-19T15:03:00Z",
    "signed_by": "redwood-ops@redwood.com"
  }

Jordan — any security notes to add on key exchange or notarization?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Export Operations, Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly — that level of detail is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we mark this as acceptable for our security review: 

1) Do the NDJSON exports include full request headers (user-agent, ip, forwarded_for) or are those parsed into metadata fields? We need source IP for our internal forensic correlation.
2) For the HMAC manifest signing, can Acme use its own verification key rather than Redwood's HMAC (i.e., Redwood signs and also provides an unsigned manifest that we sign/verify on our side)?

If you can confirm those two points and we get the attachments, we can proceed to mark the RFP item as satisfied and drop it into our procurement checklist.

Regards,
Tom Wu
Senior Security Engineer, Acme Corporation

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Tom Wu <tom.wu@acmecorp.com>, Aisha Patel <legal-requests@acmecorp.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: RFP: Schedule for retention handback + sample export

Tom — quick answers:

- NDJSON: the exports include parsed metadata columns plus a raw_headers field. That raw_headers field contains the original request headers (base64-encoded) so you can recover user-agent and x-forwarded-for information for correlation. We can also provide a parsed IP column if you prefer it in plaintext (we normally mask IPs to a /24 unless the customer requests full precision and signs a retention exception).

- Manifest signing: yes — we can provide both: the Redwood-signed manifest (HMAC) and an unsigned manifest that Acme can sign with your verification key. During onboarding we can exchange public keys or perform an ephemeral key exchange for the export.

We'll upload the attachments to the Drive link and I will open a HubSpot ticket (ACME-5562) that tracks the signed SLA addendum. If Acme is comfortable with this wording, Kimberly will schedule the sample export to your preferred transfer method (please tell us S3 vs SFTP).

Next steps:
1) Acme confirms transfer method
2) We schedule a 1-hour window for the sample export (Kimberly will propose 2 slots in the spreadsheet)
3) We exchange verification keys for the manifest signature

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if helpful.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
